title: Scarlet Monastery
body: The Scarlet Monastery stands in the hills of northeastern Tirisfal, above the gardens where the Scarlet Crusade keeps its watch. Before the plague it was a house of Lordaeron's faithful, where paladins trained and scholars studied. The Crusade made it a fortress and its great seat in the glades. Four ways lead in from the vestibule: to the graveyard, the library, the armory and the cathedral. Commander Mograine leads its soldiers, but its true master is said to be High Inquisitor Whitemane.

parts.body: Raleigh the Devout served the Crusade proudly until he watched the monastery's zealots lose their hold on reality, counting anyone without the tabard as plagued and torturing innocents for it.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Scarlet_Monastery_(original): northeast corner of Tirisfal Glades; a seminary taken by the Crusade after the Third War; the pre-Cataclysm official description (once a proud bastion of Lordaeron's priesthood, a center for learning and enlightenment; converted into a stronghold of the Crusade; outsiders seen as potential carriers of the plague; Scarlet Commander Mograine commands a large garrison of fanatically devoted warriors; the true master is High Inquisitor Whitemane, a fearsome priestess)

title: The Graveyard
body: The Graveyard wing begins in the Chamber of Atonement, a cruel name. Scarlet torturers work there among undead captives, urging them to confess and be set free, though one admits he does not care what is said: he simply enjoys inflicting pain. Beyond lies the Forlorn Cloister, where restless spirits drift between the graves, and at its far end stairs lead down into the crypts of Honor's Tomb.

title: The Library
body: The Library wing runs through the Huntsman's Cloister, where Houndmaster Loksey keeps the hounds the Crusade uses to hunt its enemies, to the Gallery of Treasures and the Athenaeum. The books laid out there are histories of the world, from the War of the Ancients to the troll wars, and in the farthest hall Arcanist Doan, a mage of the Crusade, keeps the histories of the Scourge.

parts.body: One of its books, Rituals of Power, came by a strange road: the Magus Tirth, a scholar ruined by ale and wagers, sold the last copy to one of the Scarlet clergy to pay his debts.

title: The Armory
body: The Armory wing is where the Crusade drills and arms its soldiers, through the Training Grounds, the Footman's Armory and the Crusader's Armory, among crates of armor and weapons. At the far end a heavy door opens on the Hall of Champions, where plaques honor the order's heroes and its living champion, Herod, waits with a great axe.

title: The Cathedral
body: The Cathedral wing is the heart of the monastery. Its way leads through the Chapel Gardens to the doors of the Crusader's Chapel, and its guards are the order's best, for this road leads to those who command the rest. Within the chapel abbots, monks and champions keep the nave, and at its far end Commander Mograine stands before the door of the High Inquisitor.

title: High Inquisitor Whitemane
body: High Inquisitor Whitemane is a priestess of the Light and, by every account, the true master of the Scarlet Monastery, a fearsome woman who directs the Crusade's work from within its walls. She keeps to her chambers behind the Crusader's Chapel. Scarlet Commander Mograine, who leads the monastery's soldiers, guards her door, and no one reaches her except past him.

parts.body: When Mograine fell, Whitemane raised him from death with a word, and he rose at her side. The order sworn to purge the dead has a high inquisitor who calls them back.

title: High Inquisitor Fairbanks
body: Behind a secret door off the Crusader's Chapel, opened by a torch upon the wall, a hidden room keeps High Inquisitor Fairbanks from the chapel's eyes. He bears the same title as the monastery's mistress, but he is undead, one of the very dead the Crusade has sworn to destroy, and he fights for the Crusade still. Why he lingers in that hidden place, the monastery does not say.
